post.description:
A file up to 20 MiB: image, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, text, HTML or audio. The type is read
from the bytes. The file stays unsent until a message carries it.

delete.description: Only a file that no message carries yet.

get.description:
The bytes, shown in place when a browser can show them safely (HTML never is), with
byte ranges so that audio can be played and sought on every browser. A range is cut by the
database; a refused range reads nothing.

The client kept a personal calendar link out of its queue; the thread asks the student whether

post.description:
Switches the source off, reversibly: its tasks stop, there is no sync, and its classes, tasks,
courses, grades, people, news and documents leave every view; nothing is deleted.

Switches a disabled source back on: it returns to the status it had and its data is shown
again; a source that syncs is refreshed at the next tick.

A fresh ticket for the screen this connection's login is waiting on.

Call it right before connecting and again on every reconnect: the ticket in the `login`
block is only a fast path, it expires after a minute.

put.description: User-supplied tokens (Moodle token, iCal URL, API key). Never returned back.

post.description:
Answers a block. A secret input goes straight into the Vault (`transient`, 10 minutes);
only the fact of the answer is stored. A second answer to the same block is `409`.

get.description:
text/event-stream: status | block | block_update | error | done; resume by Last-Event-ID.

Only the owner of the job may listen. The stream replays the buffered events after
`Last-Event-ID`, then follows the job until it ends; `: keepalive` every 15 seconds.

204.description: The job has ended and nothing is newer than Last-Event-ID

post.description: Run a version as a canary; it becomes activatable only after a successful canary.
Create and attach a playbook record; versions are added separately.

schema.title: Response List Source Versions Api V1 Sources  Source Id  Playbook Versions Get

post.description: Add an inactive version; `activate` requires a successful canary of that version.
Try a candidate spec/code (or the active version) without changing the source status.

Run a candidate spec/code or a version; on `activate` persist it as the new version first.

The candidate is written as an inactive version, its canary result is stored, and only a
successful run is activated. A failed candidate stays for inspection and changes nothing.
Run the active (or the named) version; the runner records freshness and state itself.

post.description:
A recording up to 5 MiB and three minutes → the recognised text. The recording is kept
nowhere: not in the database, not in a file, not in a log. `language` is an ISO 639-1 code
(Russian by default); `durationMs` is what the page measured: the daily limit is charged by
the length the provider measures, so a false claim does not help.
